facts.raw_span: 2 days of left orbital pain
hypertension controlled with lisinopril
several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/400 OS
Edematous, hyperemic left eyelids
Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Normal intraocular pressure
Normal fundi on both sides
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains; later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes
Increased abscess size with globe compression
diffusion-weighted imaging showed acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve

concepts.why: The patient has a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes.
The patient has edematous, hyperemic left eyelids, diffuse limitation in extraocular movements, and a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding.
The patient has visual acuity loss in the left eye and diffusion-weighted imaging showed acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve.
The patient has cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes.
The patient has a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and increased abscess size with globe compression.
The patient has several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis and a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding.

rationales.F01: Left orbital pain is a non-specific symptom that could be related to various conditions, including orbital cellulitis.
rationales.F03: Epiphora without prior dacryocystitis suggests a possible lacrimal system disorder, which could be related to acute dacryocystitis.
rationales.F04: Visual acuity of 20/400 OS suggests significant vision impairment, which could be related to orbital cellulitis or optic neuritis.
rationales.F05: Edematous and hyperemic left eyelids are indicative of an infectious or inflammatory process, such as orbital cellulitis or abscess.
rationales.F06: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye suggests an orbital condition, such as orbital cellulitis or abscess.
rationales.F09: Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding is highly suggestive of acute dacryocystitis and orbital cellulitis.
rationales.F10: Gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes, suggests a streptococcal infection.
rationales.F11: Increased abscess size with globe compression is highly suggestive of an orbital abscess.
rationales.F12: Diffusion-weighted imaging showing acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve is highly suggestive of optic neuritis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and increased abscess size with globe compression, as shown in the imaging studies, strongly supports the diagnosis of an Orbital Abscess, which is further complicated by the findings of acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve.
